title: GeoCities Flashback — Rainbow Marquee Homepage
description: A pitch-perfect recreation of the late-1990s personal homepage: tiled pixel backgrounds, a scrolling rainbow marquee banner, Comic Sans body copy, and clip-art construction cones that treat visual chaos as a deliberate design language.
philosophy: This template exists to honor the anarchic sincerity of the early web, when amateur publishing was radical and every pixel of decoration was a personal statement. It flatly refuses the hushed Swiss grids and muted brand palettes that dominate modern decks — noise is the medium, not a mistake. It is built for speakers who want the audience laughing with them from slide one, using irony as structural scaffolding rather than accidental tone. The presenter must own the chaos; the design rewards confidence, not apology.
goodFor: Internet-culture retrospectives and web-history conference talks
Comedy or roast-style internal team all-hands
Workshop icebreakers targeting millennial and elder-Gen-Z audiences
Tech-nostalgia panels where the theme is the joke
avoidFor: Investor pitch decks or Series-A funding rounds
Chart-heavy quarterly business reviews requiring data legibility
Client-facing brand identity or strategy presentations
author: harness

examples.promptCore: The slide channels the feverish, earnest maximalism of a 1990s personal homepage — every surface is covered, every decoration is sincere, and emptiness is treated as a missed opportunity. A rainbow-gradient marquee band dominates the upper register like a neon shop sign, commanding attention before the eye even locates the title. Clip-art icons are placed with the unironic confidence of someone who considers them professional-grade embellishment. The mood is loud, proud, and deliberately pre-ironic — the chaos is the message, and the presenter is gleefully in on it.

examples.layoutNotes: Edge-to-edge tiled pixel texture covers the entire slide with zero margin relief — no breathing room is intentional. A full-bleed horizontal marquee band spans the top quarter and serves as the primary headline carrier. The deck title sits centered in the middle zone inside a visually bordered, drop-shadowed box, with a subtitle or tagline in a smaller matching box directly beneath it. Clip-art elements (construction cones, spinning stars) anchor the bottom corners symmetrically, and an 'Under Construction' badge occupies the lower-center strip.

examples.promptCore: The slide should feel like a personal homepage discovered mid-construction — vibrant, crowded, and completely earnest about its own decorative excess. Bullet points carry animated-star or pointing-hand markers; text hierarchies shout over each other through sheer decoration rather than scale. Every horizontal band competes for attention as if authored by a different excited teenager on a different Tuesday. Avoid any minimalist breathing room or clean-grid restraint — the noise is the message, not a flaw.

examples.layoutNotes: Full-bleed tiled pixel background with a centered content column spanning roughly cols 2–11 of a 12-col grid, mimicking a late-90s nested-table structure. Content area is subdivided into two or three horizontal bands, each separated by a rainbow gradient rule line that bleeds edge-to-edge across the column. Clip-art construction cones or spinning-star stand-ins anchor the left margin of each band, with a faux visitor-counter badge serving as the page number at bottom-center. Hierarchy is communicated through decoration density and underline/blink-style emphasis rather than size contrast alone.
